I picked up LORT on January 31st, and 96 hours later I can confidently say this game has been one of the best multiplayer experiences I’ve had in years.

For me, the only real goal in any game is simple: how fast can I go? LORT absolutely scratches that itch. The movement feels incredible. There’s something about the flow of each run that makes you want to optimize everything, tighter routes, cleaner execution. It feels smooth, responsive, and rewarding in a way that keeps you saying “one more run” at 1 a.m.

What really stands out is that even though we’re technically repeating the same mission structure, no two runs ever feel the same. Different chaos, different decisions, different mistakes, different clutch moments. That unpredictability keeps it fresh every time.

And the fact that it supports 8 players? That’s the magic. Most games cap your group or split you up. LORT lets all of us pile in together. The majority of my 96 hours has been spent laughing, yelling, and occasionally getting roasted by my own friends. It’s been the perfect evening game, something we can all hop into, chill, compete a little, and just enjoy each other’s company.

Honestly, the biggest reason I love this game isn’t just the gameplay it’s that it brought our friend group back together around one shared experience. In a season of life where everyone’s busy, that matters more than anything.

I’m genuinely excited to see how the developers continue to grow and support this game. If the future updates build on what’s already here, this could easily become a staple in our rotation for a long time.

9.4/10 — Only docking 0.6 points because I’d prefer skipping being called a dumbasses lol.

Game is genuinely a blast. The key is learning to clear camps quickly and efficiently for attributes- otherwise the map boss will introduce you to the respawn screen in a very personal way. Ranger with a full attack speed build feels borderline illegal. You will shred.

Life sustain/life steal is the most impactful perk by far. Dying in the first map or two can haunt you later, especially when you’re limping around at 1 HP wishing you had that chunk of health you can no longer recover. Ask me how I know.

It’s early access, so it’s not fully polished or balanced yet, but the potential is huge. An 8-player co-op game is something I didn’t realize I needed. There’s nothing like a full lobby in voice comms, eight grown adults panic-screaming while trying to clear camps. Peak gaming.

Really hoping the devs stick with it and keep listening to community feedback, because this could turn into something special.

Also, sniper mobs are basically running ESP aimbot. The first time you lose all your progress on the second-to-last map because one of them flicked you across the screen… you’ll understand.

I'd say for $20, there are definitely better games. In fact, I think this is probably the worst game in the genre. It's not that there is anything specifically bad about it, it's just that there is very little content - upgrades feel kinda meaningless, items don't feel very impactful, etc. All your power seems to just come from blasting off camp upgrades as fast as possible. Once you beat a run once, there pretty much isn't a reason to keep playing. 

You can go buy RoR2, Gunfire Reborn, or a plethora of other multiplayer action roguelikes for around the same price and get a way better bang for your buck.

This is a regret purchase on my part, and I think this game doesn't deserve your money until there is substantially more content - it was released into early access way, way too early. If you look at the reviews, both negative and positive, you'll notice a vast majority of the playtime is 20 hours or less.

It has potential, but it needs a lot of work and a lot of time to cook. I'd stay away from this for a long while.

What a gem! LORT nails that Risk of Rain 2 energy but adds a fantasy twist and supports up to 8 players. The core loop is addictive: fight hordes, loot crazy items, stack bonkers buffs until your character is absurdly overpowered. Power-ups like Nah’s Barrier or Boomer’s Blessing turn you from goblin tickler to god slapper, and the variety (different weapons, classes, quests that alter the map/enemies/bosses) keeps every run feeling unique. Combat is smooth, and the humor in item names and overall vibe is spot-on. It's Early Access, but the foundation is rocksolid, tons of replayability, and the devs clearly care about the community (roadmap looks promising). If you're into co-op action roguelites, do yourself a favor and dive in. 10/10 chaotic fun!

reviews.review:
10 hours in, played primarily in co-op with a friend. Difficulty scaling is way off, second boss is really challenging, with his little purple minions. In 10hrs managed to get to the third stage only once.. Can definitely be skill issue, although we beat many games on hardest difficulties, and usually its fun.
Rune progression is ridiculous, in 10hrs we've barely upgraded our characters, extra two flasks, some speed, and armor, that is it. No progression, or feeling that you get better stats. 
During the run, random map gen, is heavily influenced by the party you are in, if you are a party of two, e.g. str and int, you will see the whole map in green (agility) stat camps, totally screwing you up.. we've ended up running some weird builds, to take advantage of it.
At the end of the day, there is no desire to come back to it, as you know it will be unbalanced, and difficulty will just scale through the roof, without meaningful way to influence that from your side.
I do not recommend it in its current form.

Overall 5/10 (for now)

Lort is a solid game, and it's just the right level of punishing to be fun until you get to the end. Unfortunately though, in its current state, I think it lacks the polish and replay value that it would need to be in the same league as the great modern rogue-lites. I think a big piece of this is the items. While the higher tier items are really fun and make an immediate noticeable affect on the gameplay and your current build, many of the lower tier items are boring and forgettable, often marginally increasing stats. The game would be far more engaging with a smaller more refined item pool. While the shops are cool and add a little potential for build customization, I would love to see the devs add some sort of (item printer) or trading system that could really help you weed out the stuff that doesn't make a difference in your build. Half of the fun of this genre is breaking the game with busted item strats and clever strategizing. Lort has the potential to make this happen, it just needs a little work. 

I know this review sounds negative, but I genuinely had an awesome time playing Lort with friends while it held my attention. I love the quirky art style, fast paced gameplay and enemy variety offered here. While it feels a little unfinished in its current state, I think it has a lot of potential and I'm looking forward to revisiting it once it's finished!
